waivers.reason: MODEL LIMITATION, not a board defect, and NO GEOMETRY CAN PASS IT. check_thermal models theta_JA(A) = 55 + (174-55)*exp(-A/350) for 1oz/2-layer and CLAMPS credited copper at A_SAT = 645 mm2, so its 2-layer floor is 73.85 C/W against this board's 65 C/W target - a mathematically perfect hole-free 645 mm2 still rises 73.85 C. Verified in the checker source, and independently confirmed by a 22-candidate measured aspect study (reports/aspect-study/): across every aspect from 1.00 to 2.55 the best achievable rise was 76.01 C. The board delivers 1088.960 mm2 of contiguous F.Cu +3V3 pour on the tab (ONE island, 0 mm2 orphaned, 601 mm2 credited, r20 1015.854 and r25 1088.538 both above the 1000 mm2 design floor), measured post-routing. Two independent vendor sweeps keep improving exactly where the model stops crediting copper: AMS1117 Table 1 (p5, 1/16in FR-4, 1 oz - the same board class) gives 65 C/W at 1000 mm2 top-side and 55 C/W at 2500 mm2, and TI's LM1117 Table 9-2 (p18-19) gives 66 C/W at 645 mm2 top-only; they BRACKET rather than agree, being measured at different areas. AMS p5 also states the spreading copper need not be electrically connected to the tab, so the continuous B.Cu GND plane beneath contributes dielectrically even though a live VOUT tab cannot be via-stitched to it. Both sources are cited WITH their own hedges: LM1117 section 9 opens (p14) with TI's note that these application sections are 'not part of the TI component specification, and TI does not warrant its accuracy or completeness', and AMS Table 1 calls itself 'a rough guideline... some experimentation will be necessary'. Honest reading: theta_JA ~60-65 C/W, Tj ~110-115 C at 1.00 W and Ta 50 C, against a 125 C limit. The target was deliberately NOT softened to 75 C/W to recolor this gate - 75 would state Tj <= 125 C, i.e. zero margin. SETTLED AT BRING-UP by a thermocouple on the tab at 500 mA (reports/assembly-notes.md, first-article check 2).

waivers.reason: HEURISTIC MIS-ATTRIBUTION, confirmed against the board topology. check_current charges every transition via the whole net's 0.515 A and wants >=1 via per 0.5 A. The load return does not flow through these vias at all: it goes J2's GND pin -> B.Cu GND plane -> J1's GND pin, and BOTH are through-hole screw terminals whose pins penetrate every layer directly. The GND stitch vias carry only U1's quiescent current and the two capacitors' ripple - milliamps. Independently, a 0.3 mm barrel at 20 um plating is ~0.019 mm2 of copper against 0.0090 mm2 for the 0.2575 mm track in 1 oz feeding the same node, so one via already exceeds its own trace. Note the specific shape of the remaining findings: U1 pin 1 HAS two barrels 1.99 mm apart, which cluster as one 2-via transition and pass; C2 pin 2 also has two, but 4.88 mm apart on the pad's long axis, so they read as two separate 1-via transitions. Tightening C2's pair to satisfy the check would DESTROY the redundancy it exists for - C2 is the compensation element and losing its return removes the loop's ESR zero. check_current's own message carries the qualifier 'advisory: plane-fed rail, per-cluster current unattributed'. Advisory severity; does not fail the gate - waived so it is an explicit ruling rather than recurring noise.

waivers.reason: ISSUE 4 - AUDIT-TRAIL entry for a check that is SUPPRESSED rather than waived. check_thermal computes need_vias = (dt/power) < theta_ja(A_SAT) -> 65 < 73.85 -> True, and would emit a thermal_vias warning for len(vias) < min_vias; constraints.json sets thermal[0].min_vias = 0, so the test becomes 0 < 0 and NOTHING is emitted. The engineering is correct and must not change: U1's tab pour is +3V3 while B.Cu is a continuous GND plane, so a stitching via there is a SHORT, not a heat path (verified record linear-regulator-live-tab-thermal-vias); the far-side copper works dielectrically instead (AMS1117 p5), and the board carries ZERO +3V3 vias by construction. The defect was only that a deliberate engineering decision was made INVISIBLE in the gate record by a constraint value. This entry makes it visible and would catch the violation if min_vias were ever raised without revisiting the reasoning.

waivers.reason: ISSUE 2 - TOOLING BLOCK, mitigated in assembly rather than in copper. J2 pin 1 (+3V3) is solid-connected to the thermal pour and is a through-hole screw terminal hand-soldered after PCBA; a hand iron cannot easily heat a pin sunk into ~1089 mm2 of 1 oz copper. Per-pad thermal relief is the correct fix and CANNOT BE APPLIED BY ANY ALLOWED SCRIPT: the only zone_connect call in the skill is planes_gen's ZONE-WIDE SetPadConnection, route_edit is add_track/add_via/remove, place_edit is footprint+text. The one scripted workaround - a small higher-priority thermal zone over the pad - is refused by planes_gen's unconditional >=80% existing-fill guard. The remaining option is a raw (zone_connect 1) edit, which the hard rule 'scripts own all writes' forbids, and that rule is not worth breaking for a hand-solder joint on a qty-5 bench board. COST MEASURED on a scratch copy so this is a tooling block and not a cost objection: DRC 0/0, pour stays ONE island, zone fill loses 5.363 mm2, and check_thermal's credited area is BIT-IDENTICAL either way. MITIGATION: reports/assembly-notes.md and the BOM-full.csv Instructions column both tell the assembler to preheat and use a >=60 W iron with real thermal mass on J2 pin 1, and name a cold joint there as the most likely assembly defect on this board. Zone-wide 'thermal' is NOT an option: it would relieve U1's TAB and cripple the heat path this board is built around.

waivers.reason: ISSUE 3 - loss of intended design margin, NOT a fab violation, and not this board's to fix. The board is fabricated at 0.127 mm copper clearance rather than the 0.2 mm its netclasses declare, because the unconditional aiee_clearance_floor DRU rule (min 0.127 mm) outranks netclass clearance in KiCad's resolution order. PROVEN rather than inferred: measured pad-to-pour gap is 0.127 mm on every isolated pad, which is only reachable if the floor governs - had the netclass 0.2 mm won, no gap could be below 0.2. 0.127 mm IS the JLC 2layer_1oz floor, so the board is manufacturable exactly as built, and on a 5 V board carrying 0.5 A with no fine-pitch parts the electrical consequence is nil (IPC-2221 needs ~0.1 mm at this voltage). The fix is NOT to raise the floor: that rule encodes the FAB's capability, not the design's preference, and overloading it would be a category error that hides the real fab limit. The real fix is in rules_gen (emit netclass clearance as its own rule, or make the floor conditional), which is a pipeline change. SYSTEMIC: every board in this pipeline is currently built to the fab floor rather than to its declared netclass clearance, and nothing warns about it.

waivers.reason: ISSUE 7 - 3D model only; ZERO fabrication consequence. C2's footprint references CASE-E_L7.3-W4.3-H4.1.wrl (EIA 7343-43, 4.1 mm modelled height) while the ordered part is 293D226X9016D2TE3, case D / EIA 7343-31 (~3.1 mm max). The LAND PATTERN is correct and unaffected: 7343-31 and 7343-43 share the same 7.3 x 4.3 mm body and the same copper footprint - they differ ONLY in height, so nothing that gets manufactured is wrong. The model over-states height by ~1.0 mm, which matters only to a mechanical or enclosure check, and this board has no enclosure and no height constraint (block-only tier excludes enclosure-fit). NOT FIXED because no correct CASE-D model exists in this workspace and fabricating a plausible-looking one would be worse than a documented wrong one. Recorded in reports/assembly-notes.md so anyone who later runs a clearance study off the 3D model knows to subtract ~1 mm. Note the same pulled library also produced three separate symbol defects repaired by kicad/gen/lib_fixups.py - the model is the least of it.
